title: Free-Floating Terms and Phrases
scope: Complete list (except free-floating music phrase headings, H 1917.5) of terms and phrases authorized for use on a free-floating basis in constructing phrase headings (geographic headings, MARC 651)
general_notes: Except for free-floating music phrase headings, the construction of which is explained in H 1917.5, the terms and phrases described in this instruction sheet constitute a complete list of those that have been authorized for use on a free-floating basis in constructing phrase headings.

The phrase heading [personal name] in fiction, drama, poetry, etc. was discontinued in August 1993 and replaced by the free-floating subdivision --In literature used under names of individual persons and literary authors.

The phrase heading [name heading (except personal names)] in literature was discontinued in August 1993 and replaced by the free-floating subdivision --In literature used under names of individual families, dynasties, royal houses, corporate bodies, countries, cities, etc., and uniform titles of sacred works.

The phrase heading [name heading (except personal names)] in art was discontinued in January 1997 and replaced by the free-floating subdivision --In art used under names of individual corporate bodies and under countries, cities, etc.
The phrase headings [topic] in literature and [topic] in art are no longer free-floating and must now be individually established.

Use of commas: When constructing headings of this type based on headings that are inverted or that include a comma not enclosed within a parenthetical qualifier, place an additional comma between the basic heading and the free-floating term or phrase. Example: Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)

exceptions: Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for metropolitan areas: Jerusalem Metropolitan Area, New York Metropolitan Area, and Washington Metropolitan Area.
Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for regions: Jerusalem Region, New York Region, and Washington Region.
Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for suburban areas: Jerusalem Suburban Area, New York Suburban Area, and Washington Suburban Area.

entries.pattern: [name of geographic feature, as established in the subject authority file] Region ([geographic qualifier, if part of the name as established])
examples: Bull Shoals Lake Region (Ark. and Mo.)
entries.notes: If the feature heading is inverted or includes a comma not enclosed within a parenthetical qualifier, place an additional comma before Region (e.g., Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)).

entries.pattern: [name of river, as established in the subject authority file] Region ([geographic qualifier, if part of the name as established])
entries.notes: The use of Estuary and Valley as free-floating terms added to names of rivers, and Watershed added to names of rivers and lakes, has been discontinued. Headings for estuaries, valleys, and watersheds are now individually established. See H 800, sec. 7-9 for instructions.
